subsystems.name: Gas fermentation bioreactor
subsystems.role: house the microbes and dissolve CO2 and hydrogen into the liquid they live in.

subsystems.name: Gas supply
subsystems.role: deliver the three feeds the microbes need: carbon dioxide, hydrogen and oxygen.
parts: electrolyser making H2 and O2 from water
CO2 capture unit or tanker delivery

subsystems.name: Microbial culture
subsystems.role: the living catalyst — hydrogen-oxidising bacteria that build protein from CO2.

subsystems.name: Nutrient dosing
subsystems.role: supply nitrogen, minerals and vitamins the microbes cannot make themselves.

subsystems.name: Harvest and drying
subsystems.role: separate the biomass from the water and turn it into a stable powder.

subsystems.name: Protein extraction and texturing
subsystems.role: turn the dried biomass into ingredients that behave like meat or dairy.

subsystems.name: Cooling and utilities
subsystems.role: remove the heat the exothermic fermentation releases.

buildSteps.title: Choose and grow the strain
buildSteps.detail: Select a hydrogen-oxidising bacterium that grows fast on CO2 and is safe to eat, then expand it from frozen vials into a seed culture.

buildSteps.title: Make the hydrogen
buildSteps.detail: Use renewable electricity to split water in an electrolyser. Hydrogen is the energy source; the oxygen by-product can partly feed the reactor.

buildSteps.title: Capture carbon dioxide
buildSteps.detail: Take CO2 from a brewery, cement plant or other concentrated waste stream — or, in principle, from the air — and clean it to food-grade purity.

buildSteps.title: Run the fermentation
buildSteps.detail: Feed CO2, H2, O2 and nutrients into the bioreactor at carefully controlled ratios so gas dissolves efficiently; the culture grows continuously and is drawn off.

buildSteps.title: Harvest the biomass
buildSteps.detail: Centrifuge or filter the broth to collect the microbial cells, then wash and pasteurise them.

buildSteps.title: Dry and mill
buildSteps.detail: Dry the paste into a powder that is roughly half protein by mass, with fibre, fats and vitamins alongside.

buildSteps.title: Extract and formulate
buildSteps.detail: Separate specific proteins where needed, then bind, extrude or blend the powder into patties, nuggets, drinks or dairy-type products.

buildSteps.title: Clear regulation and scale up
buildSteps.detail: Obtain novel-food approval in each market, then move from pilot vessels to larger continuous reactors with better gas transfer.

prerequisites.why: hydrogen from electrolysis is the main cost, so the price of wind and solar power sets the price of the protein.
they supply the hydrogen and oxygen the microbes metabolise.
fermenters of tens of cubic metres run today; food-grade plants at thousands of tonnes per year are still being built.

prerequisites.tech: Carbon capture from point sources or air
prerequisites.why: a clean, affordable CO2 stream is the raw material — and capturing it is what makes the process potentially carbon-negative.
approval has been granted in a few jurisdictions, so each new market needs its own safety assessment.

pathway.milestone: pilot and first commercial plants producing microbial protein, with early novel-food approval
pathway.unlocks: real products, real safety data and a working cost curve.

pathway.milestone: plants in the tens of thousands of tonnes per year using hydrogen from dedicated renewables
pathway.unlocks: ingredient-scale supply for food manufacturers rather than tasters and niche products.

pathway.milestone: cost falling toward that of conventional protein
pathway.unlocks: use as a bulk ingredient in everyday foods, not just premium alternatives.

pathway.milestone: plants sited on captured CO2 and curtailed renewable power
pathway.unlocks: food production that stores carbon and does not compete for farmland — the carbon-negative case.
